questions.history: Change a to b with setString.
questions.prediction: The PR reports old lexical text and an updated pretty-printed value on the parent. On the merge the lexical text must contain the b literal in place of a, and parsing it must yield b.
questions.basis: Only this node was edited. A fresh parse observes what was actually emitted, independent of the in-memory node.
questions.refutation: The node returns b while the emitted unit still parses to a or fails to parse.

questions.history: Start with a and call setString with a again. Preserve unusual spaces around the assignment.
questions.prediction: Expect unchanged lexical text on both revisions. The merged same-value path must leave the spelling in place.
questions.basis: An idempotent edit changes no token. A byte-for-byte copy of the original source supplies the comparison.
questions.refutation: Formatting or literal spelling changes despite an unchanged value.

questions.history: Use a new string whose decoded characters are b, LF and double quote. Place a neighboring comment containing a in the source before setup.
questions.prediction: On the merge the printed text must be parseable, with exactly that three-character string and the unchanged neighboring comment. The node and the newly parsed literal must agree.
questions.basis: A Java string literal cannot contain an unescaped physical line break. A consumer must recover the logical characters regardless of how the printer escapes them.
questions.refutation: A double escape changes the decoded value, the print no longer parses, or the untouched comment changes.
